h1: The 5 Best Carpet Cleaners Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Carpet Cleaners Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 portable carpet cleaners under $100 scored on spot-cleaning design, suction claims, versatility and brand support.
summary: The BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose is the carpet cleaner under $100 to buy: a portable spot cleaner from a brand that has built the category. The Little Green Mini is the compact sibling for cars and stairs. Vacmaster's 400 Series handles carpet and upholstery, Starrybot adds steam, and the Uwant is the budget wildcard with an 18Kpa claim.
intro: Under $100 you are not buying a whole-house carpet cleaner. Every machine in this price class is a portable spot cleaner: a small tank, a short hose and a hand tool that attacks a stain on a rug, a stair tread or a car seat. That is a legitimate job, but treating one of these as a replacement for an upright cleaner is how buyers end up disappointed.

We ranked five portable machines that listings place in the $50 to $100 bracket and scored them on the Primea framework: cleaning format and versatility, brand support, stated suction, and value. The listings here share very little detailed data, so we leaned on what the names and categories tell us and marked every gap. Upright machines and the pricier Hoover and Shark spot cleaners fall outside the cap.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The category-defining portable spot cleaner, built for carpet, upholstery and car interiors.
products.description:
The Little Green Multi-Purpose is the machine other portable cleaners imitate, a compact unit sold in the $50 to $100 bracket for stains on carpet, stairs, upholstery and car seats. The listing calls it portable and multi-purpose and gives no tank size or suction figure.

It ranks first because it comes from a brand that has defined this niche, which means accessories, replacement parts and cleaning solutions are easy to find. The multi-purpose label also separates it from the Mini below, which is aimed at smaller jobs. The tradeoff is scale: this is a spot cleaner, so a whole living room will take many refills.

A strong fit for renters, pet owners and parents who face occasional accidents. Buy a whole-room machine if you clean large areas.
products.idealFor: Renters and families handling stains on carpet and upholstery.
products.skipIf: You want to clean entire rooms in one go.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A smaller Little Green for tight spaces and quick cleanups, from the same brand.
products.description:
The Little Green Mini shrinks the BISSELL formula into a more compact portable cleaner, again in the $50 to $100 bracket. The listing says portable and little else, so the name carries the message: smaller than the Multi-Purpose, easier to stow and easier to carry.

It ranks second because small machines mean small tanks, and small tanks mean more trips to the sink. For a car, a couple of stairs or a pet corner, that is a fair trade. Against the Multi-Purpose it shares the brand support, though the full-size version better suits households with several rooms of carpet.

A good match for apartments, cars and storage-limited homes. Larger carpeted spaces call for the bigger unit.
products.idealFor: Apartments and cars where storage and size matter.
products.skipIf: You have a lot of carpet to clean.

products.name: Vacmaster 400 Series Portable Carpet & Upholstery Spot Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A portable spot cleaner named for both carpet and upholstery, from a wet-dry vacuum maker.
products.description:
Vacmaster, a name known for wet-dry vacuums, markets the 400 Series for spot work on both carpet and upholstery, priced under $100. Naming both surfaces helps in a house with sofas and rugs.

It ranks third because the listing lists no tank, power or suction figures, and its brand has less of a following in carpet care than BISSELL's, so parts and solutions are harder to source. Against the Starrybot below, it offers a more established maker and a named two-surface purpose, but no steam.

A reasonable alternative for households that favour a vacuum-brand heritage. Verify accessories before you buy.
products.idealFor: Homes with both rugs and sofas to refresh.
products.skipIf: You want the widest accessory support.

products.name: Starrybot Portable Carpet Cleaner with Steam
products.verdict: The only machine here advertising steam, in a portable body at the low end of the tier.
products.description:
Starrybot adds steam to the portable formula, as its title states, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Heat can help loosen set-in marks and lift grease, so it is a feature worth wanting on a spot cleaner.

It ranks fourth because the listing offers no temperature, tank or suction information, and a newer brand brings no accessory or parts ecosystem to lean on. Compared with BISSELL, you lose the brand trail; compared with Vacmaster, you gain steam. It sits above the Uwant because the steam claim is at least stated and specific.

Try it if heat is the feature you want. Check warranty terms before you commit.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want steam in a spot cleaner.
products.skipIf: You need an established parts and support network.

products.name: Uwant Carpet Cleaner Machine 18Kpa Portable Carpet Cleaner for Cars
products.verdict: An 18Kpa suction claim and a car-focused name, with the least information behind it.
products.description:
Uwant advertises 18Kpa of suction on a portable carpet cleaner whose title also targets cars, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Suction is quoted in kilopascals, and a higher number should pull more water from the fibres.

It ranks last because 18Kpa is a headline claim without a tank size, a hose length or a stated warranty to back it up, and the listing leans on car use instead of home carpet. Next to BISSELL's established machines it offers a bigger-sounding number and a much thinner track record. As suction claims on small machines are rarely tested, we treat it cautiously.

Best for car interiors and small rugs where you are happy to gamble. Buy a BISSELL for anything you care about.
products.idealFor: Car interiors and small rugs on a gamble budget.
products.skipIf: You want proven performance and support.

whatMatters.detail: Portable spot cleaners carry a small water tank and a hand tool, so they excel at stains but struggle with whole rooms. Upright machines clean large areas faster but cost more and take storage space. Read the title for portable or compact, and judge whether your messes are small and occasional or large and regular.

A small tank means more trips to the sink, and a clean-water tank that is too small makes rinsing awkward. Most of these listings do not state capacity, which is itself a warning. Check the specs or manual before buying, and expect to refill several times when cleaning a stair run or a car interior.

Suction pulls dirty water out of the fibres so the carpet dries faster and does not smell. The Uwant claims 18Kpa, a number you cannot verify from a listing. Weak extraction leaves carpet soaked, so look for stated suction, a wide nozzle and owner descriptions of drying time, not marketing numbers alone. Slow drying invites musty smells, particularly on thick pile or car carpet that never gets airflow.

Steam can loosen grease and old marks, but it can also set some dyes or damage delicate fibres. The Starrybot advertises steam, while the BISSELL models rely on solution and scrubbing. Check your carpet's care label, and test heat on a hidden patch before using it on visible areas. Wool and some synthetics can shrink or discolour, so follow the manufacturer's advice for your rug.

Cleaning solution, hoses, brush heads and tanks wear out and are easy to replace for established brands. BISSELL sells plenty, while newer names may not. Before buying, search for the machine's replacement parts and solutions, and check the warranty length so a broken pump does not strand you. A cheap machine with no spare parts is effectively disposable once the hose or tank cracks.

faq.q: Can a carpet cleaner under $100 clean a whole room?
faq.a: Not comfortably. The BISSELL Little Green models and the Vacmaster are portable spot cleaners with small tanks, so a full room means many refills. Upright machines cost more but cover floors faster.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with portable cleaners?
faq.a: Soaking the carpet. A small machine like the Little Green Mini can leave fibres wet if you rinse too much, so work in small passes, extract thoroughly and open a window to speed drying.

faq.q: Is the BISSELL worth it over the Uwant?
faq.a: For most buyers, yes. The Little Green Multi-Purpose brings an established brand and easy parts, while the Uwant's 18Kpa claim is unverified and its listing says little about tank, warranty or support.

faq.q: How do I set up a portable cleaner?
faq.a: Mix water and the maker's solution in the clean tank, snap on the hose and hand tool, then try a hidden patch first to check colourfastness. With the Starrybot, test the steam setting on a small area first.
Empty and rinse both tanks after each use, clean the nozzle and let parts air dry. A BISSELL or Vacmaster machine stored with wet tanks can develop odours, so leave the lids off between jobs.

faq.q: Can I use these on car seats?
faq.a: Yes, with care. The Uwant is marketed for cars, and the BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose is built for upholstery and car interiors. Use minimal water on fabric seats and extract thoroughly.

finalTake: For most households the BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose is the right carpet cleaner under $100: portable, multi-purpose and backed by a brand with easy parts. Pick the Little Green Mini for cars and small spaces, the Vacmaster for carpet plus upholstery, and the Starrybot if you want steam. Buy the Uwant only as a gamble.
